title: refactor(enter): simplify model list pricing and health display
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Organizes pricing into Pollen access, requests per Pollen, price options and extra fees, then usage rates. Uses right-aligned values, a solid overview divider and dotted detail dividers.
- Adds registry metadata for separate context, resolution, quality and other price selectors. Omits fixed resolution from the UI. Billing rates and variant selection rules are unchanged.
- Fixes Gemini Search fees appearing among token rates without an icon; preserves prompt/query billing units.
- Adds rounded health bars with gray bars for no data, concise tooltips, model ID copy icons and consistent spacing. Model titles link to Open WebUI or Play with an arrow.
- Validation: 103 pricing/catalog/query tests, Enter typecheck, frontend build and formatting pass. Gen typecheck passed in the previous round. Local simulated health and labels are excluded.

Independent of #15273.

gist.headline: The price tags learned manners
gist.blurb: The model catalog now puts Pollen access, request costs, options, extra fees, and usage rates in a sensible little row instead of letting them mingle unsupervised. Health bars got rounder, model IDs got copy buttons, and Gemini Search fees now arrive wearing their proper icon.
gist.summary: Refactored the Enter model list to group Pollen access, requests-per-Pollen, selectable price options, extra fees, and usage rates with clearer dividers, while adding registry metadata for context, resolution, quality, and other selectors without changing billing rates or variant rules.
gist.impact: Users can scan model pricing and health more reliably, see Gemini Search prompt/query fees in the right place with an icon, copy model IDs, and open each model in Open WebUI or Play directly from its title.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy garden-market model catalog where Polli acts as a meticulous librarian, arranging labeled seed packets into clear pricing sections while a CRT robot reads rounded health gauges. Pixel flowers and code-plants represent model variants; neatly separated signs represent Pollen access, request rates, options, and usage, with a small magnifying-glass/search seed packet for Gemini Search fees.
